title: Toilet Paper skill
summary: Drives the Toilet Paper compiler: the agent writes a short source file, renders the diagram or document and checks that nothing published is older than its source.
use_when: You need a BPMN diagram, a flowchart, a RACI matrix, an icon picture or a Word document from a source file.
basis: Installs with the Toilet Paper tool and follows its version.

title: Deck and document builder
summary: Plans a deck, a presentation or a branded document with you, then writes the source that Toilet Paper compiles. A deck source becomes an editable .pptx on the company master and one HTML file with the same look; a Markdown source becomes a Word document. It also starts an app page. It asks the format, the brand and the classification first, and writes nothing before you approve the plan.
use_when: You need a presentation, a report, a memo or an internal tool page that must look like the company.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test.

title: Craft apps
summary: Installs, updates and runs a set of local Office and design apps by command line and MCP, with no admin rights: decks, documents, sheets, PDF, images, vectors, video and audio.
use_when: You want to render, convert, inspect or edit a .pptx, .docx, .xlsx, .pdf, image, video or audio file by script, or check a deck or document visually before you hand it over.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test.

title: Report builder
summary: The delivery line for a Power BI report. The idea is a mockup first: the mockup writes the specification and the contract, and a set of gates checks the delivery. What runs today is the audit of the semantic model against a curation checklist (an automated pass, an assisted review, a score per category), and a record of the steps, gates and cost of a delivery.
use_when: You want to deliver a Power BI report, or to check a semantic model before it goes into one.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test. The audit is in beta.
ships: scripts (audit, report writer, step record, session cost)
wip: The mockup first, the specification and contract it writes, and the delivery gates are in design.
The mode that scaffolds a new report from a specification is in development.

title: Design review
summary: Reviews an HTML page against a design system while the page runs in a browser, at 3 screen widths, with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility checks and a measurement of the brand tokens.
use_when: You generate a dashboard, catalog, one-pager or web deck and want to know whether it follows the brand before you deliver it.

title: QA reviewer
summary: An adversarial reviewer for a diff, a file or a decision. It runs the tests that exist, then breaks every new or changed test on purpose, line by line. A test that still passes is reported as a problem. That mutation step caught an empty test on the first free-model task.
use_when: You want a second look at a change, and a check that its new tests can fail.

title: Project coach
summary: A pocket guide for running projects, anchored in a five-phase project process and the principles of PMBOK 7, pragmatic and not bureaucratic. It prepares a person for the conversation with a human mentor and does not replace it.
use_when: You ask how to start a project, what document you need, how to run a kick-off, a status report, a RACI or a closure, or how to handle risk, change, scope and stakeholders.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test.

title: OKR cycle
summary: Runs a whole OKR cycle for a team: drafts and pressure-tests the OKRs, groups them into pillars, assigns owners, balances workload, defines a 75, 100 and 125 achievement-scoring model with weights, and generates executive one-pagers (bilingual HTML to PDF) and an Excel scorecard from a single spec file.
use_when: You plan or review OKRs, want to score achievement from 50 to 150 percent, or split objectives across people.

title: Shipper
summary: Documentation, commit and push for the last mile. It fixes the docs the change made false, commits only its own paths in a clone that several sessions share, writes a conventional commit and closes the backlog idea with a script. It never stages everything.
use_when: A change is done and you want the docs, the commit and the backlog closed in one pass.

title: Fabric app method
summary: A method to create, develop and publish an app on Microsoft Fabric Apps with its CLI, in TypeScript: prepare the machine once, create the project with the team's rules, develop with Claude or Copilot, connect it to the data, review and publish.
use_when: You start a pilot app on Fabric, connect an app to a semantic model or publish one.

title: Session handoff
summary: An end-of-session handoff. It summarizes the session into the notes vault, updates the index and log and leaves a context block, so any later Claude instance can resume without the conversation history.
use_when: You close a long session and want the next one to start where this one stopped.

title: Vault start
summary: Starts a session on a notes vault: loads the operating manual, restores the last session's context, checks the inbox and asks for the day's focus.
use_when: You open a new session and want it to know where things stand.

title: Video to vault
summary: Brings a video from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram or Vimeo into the notes vault, with the provenance written by code and the analysis proposed in the session.
use_when: You want a video saved as a sourced note.

title: Autodev runner
summary: Runs a small task on a free model inside an isolated worktree under strict limits, then checks the result by code. Claude plans and reviews with a mutation check, and a team lead step caps the work. It never pushes.
use_when: You have a small task whose test proves it, and you want a free model to make the edit under limits.

title: CDMP exam coach
summary: An adaptive exam coach for the CDMP data management certification. It makes fresh practice questions one at a time, explains all five options the way an exam forum would, and tracks performance per domain and per concept, with diagnostic reports.
use_when: You study for the CDMP exam and want practice questions or a diagnosis of your weak points.

title: Web research
summary: Web research with the source and the date, using the session's own search, with no API key and no extra cost. It answers in the chat and writes no file. A colleague's name or an internal fact never goes into the search.
use_when: You ask it to research, compare tools, or check a limit, a version, a price or a feature of a product.

title: Product coach
summary: A pocket guide for defining what to build, the counterpart of the project coach. It writes a feature spec from a problem, updates a Now, Next, Later roadmap, turns research and feedback into themes and opportunities, and runs brainstorming that diverges and then converges.
use_when: You need a feature spec, a roadmap reprioritised, user feedback synthesised or ideas to solve a problem.

title: Portfolio project copilot
summary: A copilot for project managers who work in a project portfolio tool. Its commands cover the charter, the work breakdown, the sprint and the status report, and it needs write access to a notes vault.
use_when: You manage a project in a portfolio tool and want a charter, a work breakdown, a sprint plan or a status report drafted.

title: App test personas
summary: Runs a round of tests on a desktop app with 4 test personas, 2 who know the app and 2 beginners. Each persona uses the real app in the built-in browser and writes test cases that the app's own test mode shows.
use_when: You want to test Capy with personas or feed its test mode.
